newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian real ends up 0.24 pct in seesaw trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian real ends up 0.24 pct in seesaw trade.

text.p: Brazil's real rose 0.24 percent to close at 1.0590 reais per dollar in the commercial forex market in seesaw trade, dealers said.
The local currency traded between 1.0600 and 1.0614 for most of the day, as the market tried to anticipate the Central Bank's next move.

Some dealers believed the Central Bank would only lower the real's mini-band if the supply of dollars in the market grew, as it did today. But the Central Bank did not move the band, leading many to believe a new decline would come on Monday.

The current mini-band was set on March 17 at 1.0565 to 1.0615 reais per dollar. So far this month, the mini-band has been lowered 0.52 percent. In the last few months, the mini-band had been scaled down between 0.55 percent and 0.65 percent.
Wednesday's dollar flows increased market liquidity, causing the real to strengthen to 1.0590 per dollar, traders said.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts on Wednesday showed a $230 million surplus.

Dealers did not believe the actual surplus would be so large once all transactions were registered. Still, even a small surplus would be good news because it would be the first one-day dollar surplus since March 17.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0622 per dollar, down 0.01 percent.
In the illegal parallel market, the real fell 1.33 percent to end at 1.140 reais per dollar in a thin turnover.

The parallel market has seen its dollar supply fall sharply over the past few weeks due to an ongoing probe into an alleged multi-million dollar fraud involving state and municipal bonds. Investigators suspect some parallel market dollar traders helped launder money from the illicit bond deals.
All financial markets in Brazil will be closed through Monday for the four-day Easter holiday.
